summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Indology, Douglas Ober studied at the University of Washington and completed a PhD under Harjot Oberoi at the University of British Columbia (attested 2016).

Douglas Osto, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Grinnell College, Harvard University, the University of Washington, and SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel. In 2005, he became a Senior Lecturer at Massey University.

Focusing on linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology, Douglas Q. Adams studied at the University of Chicago (~1968–1972) and served at the University of Idaho from around 1974 to 2011.

Scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology Douglas S. Duckworth earned his BA at James Madison University and his PhD under Jeffrey Hopkins at the University of Virginia. He held posts at Rangjung Yeshe Institute and East Tennessee State University.
Dragana Majhen specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed a Master's degree under thesis advisor Albert Welter at the University of Manitoba (attested 2010).

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology, Dragomir Dimitrov earned his PhD at the University of Marburg under Michael Hahn. He held posts at the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project, Marburg (attested 2002–2023), and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Dramdul works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Director at the China Tibetology Research Center (attested 2004–2012) and editor-in-chief for Sanskrit Texts from the Tibetan Autonomous Region (attested 2013–2020).
Drodul Dorji Tenzin studied under Dudjom Rinpoche and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Drodul Pawo Dorje studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Ayu Khandro, and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Drolkar Chungchung studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Specializing in Tibetology, Drolma earned an M. Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008).
Drubwang Shakya Shri studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and taught Lobsang Phuntshok Lhalungpa.

id: P:Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé
summary: Drukpa Ku Chen Chöying Rolwé Dorjé studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and he taught Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.
Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje studied under Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and he taught numerous disciples, including Sogyal Rinpoche and Keith Dowman.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Dudjom Rinpoche studied at Mindrolling and Dorje Drak Monasteries under Sera Khandro and others. He founded the International Nyingma Society and taught many students, including Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Sangharakshita.

Indologist Dugald Mackichan studied at the University of Glasgow, Leipzig, and Berlin. He served as Principal of Wilson College, Mumbai (1878–1920) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1888–1890).

Duncan Forbes, working in linguistics and Indology, studied at Perth Grammar School and the University of St Andrews. He taught at Calcutta Academy, became Professor of Oriental languages at King's College London (1837–1861), and worked at the British Museum.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology, Duncan Ryūken Williams earned his PhD at Harvard University under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He held posts at Harvard, UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Dung Ngoc Duong completed a PhD at Boston University by 2001 under the supervision of Malcolm David Eckel.
